sources.title: Deep-Learning-Based Human Activity Recognition Using Wearable Sensors
sources.snippet: The observer calculates the vertical angle of the IMU sensor in real time relative to the gravity vector, and also the accelerometer and gyroscope bias values. A modern CNN-LSTM model is then selected for human activity recognition based on 8783 time samples of data obtained while doing 9 different activities.

sources.snippet: Human activity recognition (HAR) using wearable inertial sensors is increasingly vital for healthcare, rehabilitation, and pervasive computing. Yet, many state-of-the-art (SoTA) models rely on handcrafted feature engineering, heavy time-frequency transformations, or large neural networks, limiting real-time deployment on resource-constrained smartphones and wearables. sources.snippet: Leveraging explainable AI (XAI), we interpret muscle activation patterns for personalized rehabilitation insights. By unifying signal processing, efficient deep learning, and interpretability, X-LiteHAR advances real-time HAR for clinical and wearable applications.
